newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: JCI APPROVES PROJECTS WORTH 1.97 BLN RAND.
newsitem.headline: JCI APPROVES PROJECTS WORTH 1.97 BLN RAND.

text.p: New expansion projects approved in 1996 at JCI Ltd had an aggregate capital cost of nearly two billion rand, managing director Bill Nairn said on Tuesday.

Presenting the South African mining house's results for the year to June 30, 1996, Nairn said the new projects to be implemented across the gold, coal and chrome divisions would cost the company 1.97 billion rand.
These included extensive capital development at all of the group's gold mines to increase available ore reserves and exploiting the five-seam project at the Tavistock coal mine.
Actual expenditure by group operations during the past year on new or continuing capital projects amounted to 425 million rand, Nairn said.

During the year some 49 million rand was spent on exploration and new business development, primarily outside South Africa. This was expected to double to about 90 million rand in the current financial year, Nairn said.
